items.originalTitle: 梅赛德斯：资金不足，无法跟上对手升级步伐
items.summaryEn: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says the team does not have enough budget to develop its 2026 car as intensively as McLaren and Ferrari. Both rivals have made significant progress through major upgrades, while Mercedes has taken a more conservative approach.
detailZh: 梅赛德斯"没有足够的钱"来跟上对手一级方程式升级的步伐
梅赛德斯一级方程式车队负责人托托·沃尔夫表示，车队剩余的预算额度已不足以像直接竞争对手那样快速推进升级
兰多·诺里斯、迈凯伦、乔治·拉塞尔、梅赛德斯
梅赛德斯一级方程式车队领队托托·沃尔夫表示，他的车队"没有足够的钱"像迈凯伦和法拉利那样大力研发2026年的赛车。
迈凯伦和法拉利近几个月都在各自赛车上堆叠大量升级，取得了显著进步，这使两队都成为了能多次赢得分站冠军的车队。
与此同时，梅赛德斯采取了更为保守的升级计划，自五月的加拿大大奖赛以来几乎没有重要更新，这削弱了布拉克利车队最初的统治地位。
在迈凯伦的卫冕世界冠军兰多·诺里斯于赞德沃特赢得2026年连续第二场大奖赛胜利后，沃尔夫表示，梅赛德斯无法在2026年的研发竞赛中与竞争对手的投入相匹敌。
当被Motorsport.com问及，鉴于迈凯伦的迅速进步，这些研发决定是否开始让人越来越不安时，沃尔夫表示，由于车队对2.15亿美元预算上限的分配方式，他们在这方面束手无策。
"我们没有钱在赛车上投入研发。我之前说过，根据我们关于何时能带来最大升级以及如何优化锦标赛积分的计算，我们正试图在整个赛季中平均分配这些研发。但我们做不到的事情就是做不到,"这位奥地利人表示。
"这就是为什么这是一场研发竞赛。如果你带来一项升级，每支顶级车队都能从中获得至少零点几秒的进步，而这就是你会损失的东西。所以，是的，这段旅程比年初时更加艰难了。"
当被追问为什么梅赛德斯没有足够的成本上限预算来升级、而迈凯伦和法拉利却有时，他回答说："嗯，到了赛季末你就会知道，他们是否还能像现在这样往赛车上部署这么多东西。
"有些人的策略可能不同，会在年初和年中花得更多，而不是在赛季末。"
在F1十月初重新回到海外赛场（从在马来西亚举办的巴林大奖赛开始——原文如此）之前，梅赛德斯预计不会为W17带来任何重大升级。
沃尔夫指出，如果梅赛德斯在动力单元的可靠性问题上没有那么多挣扎，局面本会大不相同。这一问题到目前为止已经让安东内利和拉塞尔损失了几十分，而且后续还会导致发车罚退。
"我们在前期和初始研发上是否花得太多了？我不这么认为，"他补充道，"我只是觉得我们是一个具有一定规模和基础设施的组织。"
"从这方面来说，我们当时有一辆非常快的车。由于可靠性问题，我们损失了大约50到100分。这本来会让我们比今天拥有更大的优势。除此之外，我们只是继续按照原本的计划以及财务现实对我们的要求去执行。"
detailEn: Mercedes "hasn't got the money" to keep up with rival F1 upgrades
Mercedes Formula 1 chief Toto Wolff claims the team doesn't have enough budget allocation left to fast-track upgrades like its direct rivals
Lando Norris, McLaren, George Russell, Mercedes
Mercedes Formula 1 team principal Toto Wolff says his squad "hasn't got the money" to develop its 2026 car as much as McLaren and Ferrari are doing.
Both McLaren and Ferrari have made significant progress in recent months by piling on upgrades to their respective cars, which has turned both into multiple race winners.
Meanwhile, a more conservative upgrade plan at Mercedes, with little significant updates since May's Canadian Grand Prix, has eroded the Brackley squad's initial dominance.

Speaking after McLaren's reigning world champion Lando Norris took his second consecutive grand prix win of 2026 in Zandvoort, Wolff said Mercedes isn't able to match what its rivals are doing in the 2026 development race.

When asked by Motosport.com if those development decisions are now starting to become increasingly uncomfortable in light of McLaren's rapid progress, Wolff said his team's hands are tied with how it has partitioned its $215m cost cap allowance.

"We haven't got the money to put developments on the car. I said before that we are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points. But we just can't do what we can't do," the Austrian said.

"That's why it is a development race. If you bring an upgrade, each of the top teams will have a couple of tenths in it, at least, and that's what you lose. So, yeah, the ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year."

When pressed on why Mercedes hasn't got the cost cap budget to bring upgrades when McLaren and Ferrari have, he replied: "Well, you will see towards the end of the season whether they are going to be able to deploy as much stuff onto the car as they do now.
"Someone might have a different strategy in spending more at the beginning and the middle of the year than towards the end."
Mercedes isn't expected to bring any significant upgrades to the W17 until F1 heads overseas again, starting with the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of October.

Wolff pointed out that the picture would have looked differently if Mercedes hadn't struggled as much with the reliability of its power unit, which has cost both Kimi Antonelli and George Russell several dozens of points thus far and will lead to grid penalties down the line.
"Did we spend too much at the beginning and the initial development? I don't think so," he added. "I just think we are an organisation with a certain size and infrastructure.

"In that respect we had a really quick car. We left between 50 and 100 points on the table due to reliability issues. That would have given us a little bit more of a gap than we have today. And other than that, we are just continuing to execute what the plan was and what the financial realities mean for us."

keyPointsEn: Both McLaren and Ferrari have become winners of multiple races.

items.originalTitle: 诺里斯不同意安东内利和拉塞尔关于F1实力排名的看法
items.summaryEn: Lando Norris has disagreed with Kimi Antonelli and George Russell's claim that McLaren now has the best car in F1, arguing that his driving is making the difference. The reigning world champion won the last two grands prix from pole after a heavily upgraded MCL40 went winless in the first 10 rounds.
detailZh: 兰多·诺里斯（诺里斯）不同意基米·安东内利（安东内利）和乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔）对F1车队实力排序的看法
梅赛德斯车队的两位车手认为迈凯伦是目前最应该击败的车队，但诺里斯认为他最近赢得的分站冠军更多是归功于他自己的驾驶水平
兰多·诺里斯（诺里斯）不认同基米·安东内利（安东内利）和乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔）所说的迈凯伦现在拥有F1最佳赛车的说法——他认为是自己的驾驶在起决定性作用。
这位卫冕世界冠军凭借大幅升级的MCL40赛车，从杆位起跑赢得了最近两场大奖赛——布达佩斯站和赞德沃特站，而该车在前10轮比赛中一胜未得。
2026年初的那些比赛被梅赛德斯主导，他们从杆位起步赢得了前六场比赛，但此后由于法拉利和迈凯伦提升了赛车性能，他们只拿到了两场胜利。
因此，积分榜领先者、周日在赞德沃特获得第二名的安东内利表示，梅赛德斯“明显”落后于迈凯伦，而在荷兰大奖赛上获得第三名的拉塞尔也同意这一说法。
当梅赛德斯这两位车手的言论被抛给诺里斯时，他说：“嗯，他们不会说他们自己，对吧？
“所以他们才是最需要击败的车队，即使他们今天刚刚被击败，所以我不认为这是真的。我觉得如果我超越基米时没被他挡住……不对，我觉得如果我当时没能超越基米，我今天就赢不了这场比赛。
安东内利，梅赛德斯车队；诺里斯，迈凯伦车队。
“这很难说，但我也知道自己在方向盘后面做得有多出色，当然，我从来不是一个爱多夸自己的人，通常恰恰总是相反。
“但这一次我想给自己一点肯定，我觉得自己比其他所有人做得都更好，我认为这也可能带来不同。”
2026赛季可以说是Norris处于最佳状态的赛季，因为尽管他没有参与总冠军争夺——目前落后Antonelli 86分——但他已经把自己的赛车包发挥到了极致。
这一点与队友皮亚斯特里的对比中显而易见——Piastri在荷兰站获得第六名，目前在积分榜上仍排第七，落后第四名的Norris 55分。
这位英国车手在两人的排位赛正面交锋中也以13比4领先（包括冲刺赛），因此Norris认为正是他的驾驶水平让迈凯伦看起来与梅赛德斯处于同一水平线。
他甚至用赞德沃特的冲刺赛进一步证明自己的观点：Russell从杆位出发一路统治比赛，而Norris只是勉强挡住了Antonelli保住第三——这位意大利车手因底板受损从第五位发车。
“我们看看昨天的情况和排位赛，”这位如今已13次赢得大奖赛冠军的车手补充道，“但我们昨天没有赢，而且我们实际上没做什么改动。不过我在自己的驾驶上下了很大功夫。我想重新比其他所有人都更有信心，而我们今天扭转了局面。”
“所以说，总的来说，我们确实有一辆和梅赛德斯非常相似的车，但我认为他们的车整体性能比我们的更好。我们在高速弯道上更有特长。7号弯和8号弯正是我今天能赢得时间的最关键的两个弯角。
“但是，你知道，如果我在昨天的排位赛中犯了一个错误，只拿到第三、第四或第五名，我就赢不了比赛，那时也就不会有人再说这些话了。所以我认为，人们之所以这么说，恰恰是因为我做得确实不错。”
detailEn: Lando Norris disagrees with Kimi Antonelli and George Russell on F1's pecking order
The Mercedes duo reckons McLaren is the team to beat, but Norris thinks his recent wins are more down to his driving
Lando Norris has disagreed with Kimi Antonelli and George Russell for saying McLaren now boasts the best car in Formula 1 - arguing it’s his driving that’s making the difference.
The reigning world champion has won the last two grands prix – Budapest and Zandvoort – from pole thanks to a heavily-upgraded MCL40, which went winless in the opening 10 rounds.
Those early races in 2026 were dominated by Mercedes, who won the first six from pole but has only taken two victories since because of Ferrari and McLaren improving their cars.
So it led to championship leader Antonelli, who finished second at Zandvoort on Sunday, saying Mercedes is “clearly” behind McLaren, and Russell agreed after finishing third in the Dutch GP.
When those comments from the Mercedes duo were therefore put to Norris, he said: “Well, they’re not going to say themselves, are they?
“So they’re the team to beat [even] if they just got beaten today, so I don’t think it’s true. I think if I didn’t get Kimi when I overtook him, I don’t think I would have won the race today.
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Lando Norris, McLaren
“It’s hard to say, but I also know how good of a job I’m doing behind the wheel, and of course, I’m never one to over-talk about myself, normally always the complete opposite.
“But for once I would give myself a little bit of credit that I feel like I’m doing a better job than everyone, and I think that can also make a difference.”
The 2026 campaign has arguably been Norris at his best because although he isn’t in the championship fight, sitting 86 points behind Antonelli, he has maximised his package.
That is evident when compared to team-mate Oscar Piastri, who finished sixth in the Netherlands to remain seventh in the standings and 55 points behind fourth-placed Norris.
The Briton is also 13-4 up in their qualifying head-to-head (including sprint races) so Norris reckons it’s his driving that’s causing McLaren to look like it’s in the same league as Mercedes.

He even used the Zandvoort sprint race to further illustrate his point, as Russell dominated from pole while Norris only just held off Antonelli for third – the Italian started fifth due to floor damage.

“We look at yesterday and in qualifying,” added the now 13-time grand prix winner, “but we didn’t win yesterday and we didn’t really change much. But I worked a lot on my driving. I want to believe more than everyone else again, and we turned things around today.

“So we certainly have a very similar car, I would say, all in all, to Mercedes, but I think they have a better all-round performing car than what we do. We are more specific in high-speed [curves]. Turn 7 and Turn 8 were just our biggest two corners where I would gain time today.

“But, yeah, you know, if I make one mistake in qualifying yesterday and P3, P4, P5, I’m not going to win, and then no one’s going to be saying these things. So the fact I’m just doing a good job is, I think, why people are saying it.
keyPointsZh: 诺里斯最近在布达佩斯和赞德沃特两场大奖赛中从杆位取胜。
大幅升级的MCL40在赛季前10场比赛中未能获胜。
keyPointsEn: Norris won the last two grands prix in Budapest and Zandvoort from pole.

items.titleZh: 法拉利解释汉密尔顿荷兰大奖赛无线电爆发：并非实验品
items.summaryZh: 法拉利车队负责人弗雷德·瓦塞尔澄清了刘易斯·汉密尔顿在荷兰大奖赛期间无线电爆发的原因。法拉利连续第二场比赛未能登上领奖台，汉密尔顿获得第四，队友夏尔·勒克莱尔第五。

items.originalTitle: 法拉利解释汉密尔顿荷兰大奖赛无线电爆发：并非实验品
items.summaryEn: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur has clarified what led to Lewis Hamilton's radio outbursts during a tough Dutch Grand Prix weekend for the Formula 1 outfit. The Scuderia finished off the podium for a second consecutive race as Hamilton took fourth with team-mate Charles Leclerc in fifth.
detailZh: 当 Hamilton 在 Dutch GP 感觉自己像“小白鼠”时，法拉利 实际上想做什么
这位七届世界冠军在周日的 F1 Dutch GP 期间多次在无线电中爆发，法拉利 已解释其意图是什么
法拉利 老板 Fred Vasseur 澄清了是什么导致 汉密尔顿 在这支 Formula 1 车队艰难的 荷兰站 周末期间在无线电中爆发
这支 Scuderia 连续第二场比赛无缘领奖台，Hamilton 获得第四，队友 勒克莱尔 位列第五——与 Budapest 的结果相反——而在周日这场 72 圈的比赛中，对 法拉利 而言决定性时刻是什么已很清楚
第一次发生在比赛中段，当时汉密尔顿刚刚超越迈凯伦车手奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里升至第五，并开始逼近速度慢得多的勒克莱尔。但由于赞德福特的赛道特性狭窄，这位七届世界冠军发现很难超车，因此呼吁车队下达指令，但指令并未到来，这让兰多·诺里斯以及梅赛德斯双雄基米·安东内利和乔治·拉塞尔得以在前方扩大优势。
“真是浪费时间的妙招啊，伙计们，干得好！”汉密尔顿讽刺地厉声说道。当勒克莱尔在第43圈——比原定时间晚了一圈——进行第二次进站时，汉密尔顿最终升至第四。
人们本以为这位英国人随后不久就会进站更换新轮胎，毕竟法拉利赛车周围的车手都这么做了，但法拉利车队却选择让汉密尔顿在外面多跑很久，这意味着他最终取得了领先。
但诺里斯和安东内利凭借更新的轮胎迅速逼近，到第53圈时，他们彼此之间的差距都在一秒之内。“你们把我当小白鼠了吗？”汉密尔顿打趣道。他几乎成了活靶子，迈凯伦和梅赛德斯分别在54圈和55圈超越了他。
这位法拉利车手基本上被蒙在鼓里，不知道自己的第二段为何如此漫长——长达30圈——直到第55圈因奥康引发的虚拟安全车，才让这位41岁的车手得以用掉硬胎，换上一套全新的软胎。
“我们当时不想告诉他策略，因为不想向竞争对手泄露，”Vasseur说道。“我们想让他留在赛道上直到最后，我认为那会是正确的决定。
“Charles本应进站。我们多跑了一圈，出现了一些混乱。我对此并不担心。所有人都会在简报会上回来。他们会对比赛有清晰的了解。
“Charles一度对轮胎配方有些沮丧。我认为每个人对配方都有点困惑。Norris在第一次起步时[红旗前]用的是中性胎，然后他换成了软胎。
今天三种化合物之间的差距非常微小。很难对策略有清晰的判断。有时候，我们不得不改变策略或做出调整，因为我们正试图向其他人学习。对他们来说，这有点令人沮丧。
所以，汉密尔顿赛后媒体采访环节中讨论的焦点显而易见，期间他呼吁法拉利要有‘更好的执行’。他援引老东家梅赛德斯作为灵感来源，考虑到银箭在拉塞尔于第65圈将第二名让给安东内利时迅速下达的车队指令——当时这位积分榜领跑者在虚拟安全车下换上了软胎，而这位英国人则留在外面用硬胎。
拉塞尔最初告诉比赛工程师马库斯·达德利，‘我们丢掉了双领奖台’，因为汉密尔顿正在逼近他的前队友，但这位梅赛德斯车手守住了第三名，并在赛后表示这次交换是正确的决定。
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利，乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯
要不是之前与勒克莱尔的那场闹剧，汉密尔顿认为他本有更好的机会在后期争夺领奖台，瓦塞尔也附和了这些评论，称“今天的执行不够好”。
“赛后你总是可以说，在第46圈做会更好，”这位法国人补充道。“问题是，当刘易斯追回到查尔斯身后时，我们本以为他会进站。
“然后我们车后有个人。我们让他再多跑一圈。你不能让他在直道上多跑一圈还要交换位置。这并不容易。如果我现在回看这场比赛，我能看到差异。主要问题是我们没有告诉刘易斯，我们预计他会坚持到最后。这不是推进的问题。”
这一结果使法拉利落后领头羊梅赛德斯87分，领先第三名迈凯伦75分，后者由诺里斯连续从杆位获胜，还剩11站比赛。
detailEn: What Ferrari actually meant to do when Hamilton felt like a "guinea pig" in Dutch GP
The seven-time world champion had various radio outbursts during Sunday's F1 Dutch GP and Ferrari has explained what its intention was
Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur has clarified what led to Lewis Hamilton’s radio outbursts during a tough Dutch Grand Prix weekend for the Formula 1 outfit.

The Scuderia finished off the podium for a second, consecutive race as Hamilton took fourth with team-mate Charles Leclerc in fifth – the reverse of Budapest – and it is clear what the defining moments were for Ferrari during Sunday’s 72-lap contest.

The first occurred midway through when Hamilton had just overtaken McLaren driver Oscar Piastri for fifth and started closing in on a much slower Leclerc. But due to the tight nature of Zandvoort, the seven-time world champion found it difficult to overtake and was therefore calling for team orders which didn’t arrive, allowing Lando Norris, plus Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, to increase their advantage up ahead.

“Great way of wasting time guys, good job!” snapped a sarcastic Hamilton, who eventually took fourth when Leclerc made his second pitstop on lap 43 – one tour after he was initially supposed to do so.

The assumption was that the Briton would come in for fresh tyres shortly afterwards, considering those around the Ferrari cars did the same, but the Scuderia opted to keep Hamilton out for much longer, which meant he eventually took the lead.

But Norris and Antonelli rapidly closed in on fresher tyres, and by lap 53 they were all within a second of each other. “Are you using me as a guinea pig?” quipped Hamilton, who was practically a sitting duck as the McLaren and Mercedes respectively overtook him on laps 54 and 55.

The Ferrari driver was essentially left in the dark as to why his second stint was so long - 30 laps - and it required a lap 55 virtual safety car caused by Esteban Ocon for the 41-year-old to ditch his hard tyres for a fresh set of softs.

“We didn't want to tell him the strategy at this stage because we didn't want to disclose it to the competitors,” said Vasseur. “We wanted to keep him on track until the end, I think it would have been the right call.
“Charles was supposed to pit. We extended one lap and it was a kind of confusion. I'm not worried about this. Everybody will be back in the briefing. They will have a clear picture about the race.

“Charles was a bit frustrated at one stage about the compound. I think everybody was a bit lost about the compound. Norris started with mediums on the first start [before the red flag], then he moved to softs.

“The difference between the three compounds was very marginal today. It was difficult to have a clear picture on the strategy. Sometimes, we have to change the strategy or adapt, because we are trying to learn from the others. For them it's a bit frustrating.”

So it’s obvious what dominated discussions in Hamilton’s post-race media session, during which he called for Ferrari to have ‘better execution’. He cited his former team Mercedes as inspiration, considering the late team orders the Silver Arrows quickly deployed as Russell handed second to Antonelli on lap 65 after the championship leader took softs under the VSC, while the Briton stayed out on hards.

Russell initially told race engineer Marcus Dudley that “we’ve lost a double podium” as Hamilton closed in on his former team-mate, but the Mercedes driver held on for third and post-race said the swap was the correct decision.
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, George Russell, Mercedes

Had it not been for the earlier fiasco with Leclerc, Hamilton reckons he’d have had a better shot at claiming a late podium and Vasseur echoed those comments, claiming “the execution today was not that good”.
“You can always say after the race that it would have been better to do it on lap 46,” the Frenchman added. “The story is that, when Lewis came back on Charles, we were expecting him to pit.

“Then we had someone in the shadow of the car. We asked him to do one lap more. You can't ask him to do one lap more and to swap positions in the straight line. It's not so easy. If I have a look at the race now, I can see the difference. The main issue is that we didn't tell Lewis that we were expecting him to go to the end. It was not a matter of pushing.”
The result leaves Ferrari 87 points behind leader Mercedes and 75 ahead of third-placed McLaren, which has taken consecutive wins from pole via Norris, with 11 rounds remaining.

items.titleZh: 赞德福特赛道完美告别：荷兰大奖赛我们学到了什么
items.summaryZh: 赞德福特赛道（暂时）为F1献上了一场精彩的告别战，荷兰大奖赛在领跑集团充满真正的悬念，并出现了一些可能影响后续分站的车队积分榜意外变化。
items.originalTitle: F1荷兰大奖赛落幕：赞德福特赛道完美告别，我们学到了什么
items.summaryEn: Zandvoort enjoyed a great Formula 1 send-off (for now) as the Dutch Grand Prix delivered genuine intrigue at the front and some surprising championship developments that could echo through the coming races.
detailZh: 赞德福特享受了一场盛大的F1告别仪式（至少目前如此），荷兰大奖赛在领跑集团中呈现出真正的悬念——并且总冠军争夺形势出现了一些令人意外的发展，这些可能会在接下来的比赛中持续发酵。
以下是我们在周日的比赛中总结出的主要收获。
梅赛德斯没有足够的资金与迈凯伦抗衡
尽管梅赛德斯的竞争对手们——尤其是迈凯伦——近来显得越来越强势，但F1界在很大程度上一直默认，迈凯伦相对于梅赛德斯的进步在很大程度上只是研发周期不同所致，并且很快就会被即将到来的W17升级套件所抵消。
情况可能仍然如此，但车队领队托托·沃尔夫（Toto Wolff）突然非常强硬地声明，梅赛德斯“没有钱”——即成本上限额度——来跟上迈凯伦的升级速度。
“由于可靠性问题，我们损失了50到100分，否则我们的领先优势会比现在更多一点，”沃尔夫还辩称。
“除此之外，我们只是在继续执行原定的计划，以及财务现实对我们的意义。”
也许梅赛德斯本来就打算在年初大干一场——如果是这样的话，沃尔夫提到的那些丢失的分数可能确实具有额外的意义。
过去几年里，兰多·诺里斯（诺里斯）因其比赛技术中的一些粗糙之处，尤其是在与马克斯·维斯塔潘（维斯塔潘）争夺总冠军时，受到了不少批评。
但周日他在赞德沃特表现出色，为本就非常强势的赛季再添光彩，而这个赛季可以说比他以往任何一个夺冠赛季都要更胜一筹。
他荷兰大奖赛夺冠的高光时刻，是在第一个弯道从外侧超越总冠军领跑者基米·安东内利（安东内利）的那次超越。
"毫无疑问，他现在在驾驶中展现出更强的果断性——超越安东内利的那次动作，我认为正是这一点的一个非常好的展示，"迈凯伦车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉（Andrea Stella）说。
"他正展现出更多的自信，这很有趣，我相当喜欢这一点。"
"自信有时并不表现为最具攻击性。有时候你很自信，但你会想，比如：'你知道吗？我现在不会去争斗，因为在这场争斗中我可能会输。这是一场非常漫长的比赛，比赛结束时再见。'
"这是对你自己的手段、你的实力的信心，我很喜欢这一点，这意味着有时候当情况变得太冒险时，实际退让的那个人反而是你。"
"我们需要记住，在他赢得的最近两场比赛中，他都没有在第一圈守住杆位。第一圈结束时他实际上排在第二，但我没有听到或察觉到他的自信有任何衰减，就他更快这一点而言，他只是在准备自己的机会，而不是在挥霍他的自信。"
"从非技术、非运营的角度来看，果断和自信可能是他进步最大的两个特质。"
本田对新引擎有明确的优先事项
费尔南多·阿隆索（阿隆索）在荷兰大奖赛中获得第九名，这显示了阿斯顿·马丁（阿斯顿·马丁）和本田（Honda）通过赛季中升级所取得的进步。
尽管这是车队本赛季至今的最佳成绩，并且不再垫底，但车队离开赞德沃特（Zandvoort）时非常清楚，在开始考虑取得更好成绩之前，有一个关键领域需要掌控：引擎的可操控性。
2026年非常复杂的规则，加上Honda在新动力单元的燃烧特性方面不如竞争对手掌握得那么透彻，导致它难以提供一台能始终按车手意愿工作的发动机。
最大的（但不是唯一的）问题是入弯阶段，发动机可能在刹车时继续推动，或触发被拒绝的降挡，这让车手的工作变得极其艰难。
Honda已经启动了樱花的测试台架，以帮助在周末寻找改进方案，并在周六的荷兰大奖赛排位赛上首次推出了标定微调。蒙扎还将迎来进一步的变化。
在那里能有更多改进将是双重好消息。它们不仅会让车手的工作更轻松，还有助于释放更多动力。
这后一个因素至关重要，因为就目前而言，可驾驶性方面的种种难题给一个重大疑问蒙上了阴影：最新的Honda规格到底算得上多大的进步。
皮亚斯特里在太多场比赛中'差距还很大'
奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里（皮亚斯特里）在单圈速度上始终对诺里斯构成威胁：尽管全年战绩是4比13，但从平均差距来看，他们仍属于F1队友组合中差距最小的一对。
但他的大奖赛是一次格外令人警醒的经历，完赛时与队友相差半分钟的差距就是明证。
"兰多以相当大的优势赢得了比赛，所以我认为赛车状态不错，过去两个周末它都很快，我认为这两条赛道很适合这辆赛车——只是不知道为什么我一直无法发挥出它的速度," 皮亚斯特里承认。
"这不是今年第一场出现这种情况的比赛了——有些比赛表现不错，有些非常强势，但现在已经有太多次与预期相差甚远了。"
皮亚斯特里和斯特拉都强调说，实际上只有某一段特定的节——比赛中段用硬胎的那一段——造成了绝大部分的损失。
"我们没能让这套轮胎进入状态。它们一直处于抓地力极低极低的状态，而我们在第一段并没有看到这种情况," 斯特拉说。
小红牛毁了升级版阿尔派的首秀
在亨格罗林赛道，阿尔派在车手/车队积分榜第五名的争夺中被小红牛反超，而且从性能角度来看，它还落后于奥迪，沦为了F1第七快的赛车。
车队希望其在赞德沃特带来的升级——这套升级只装在加斯利的车上，科拉平托预计将在蒙扎用上——能够改变局面。
而冲刺赛的证据表明，Gasly领跑中游集团并以第八名拿到一个积分，这确实证明了升级起到了作用。
但Gasly在正赛中重复那一成绩的机会被Arvid Lindblad的小红牛车队毁掉了。
Lindblad为了车队利益坑了Gasly一把，因为他的比赛早已因在黄旗下超越阿尔派车手而被罚通过维修区而毁掉。
他在比赛中段对Gasly进行了非常顽强的防守，让霍肯伯格的奥迪和角田裕毅的小红牛得以趁机超越。
这限制了Gasly只能以第10名获得一个积分，但这位阿尔派车手表示他会在今年晚些时候复仇。
detailEn: Zandvoort enjoyed a great Formula 1 send-off (for now) as the Dutch Grand Prix delivered genuine intrigue at the front - and some surprising developments in the shape of the championship that could echo through the coming races.
Here are our main learnings from the Sunday race.
Mercedes doesn't have money to match McLaren

As increasingly potent as Mercedes' rivals - and specifically McLaren - have looked as of late, the F1 world has largely operated under the assumption that McLaren's gains on Mercedes are in large part a consequence of development cycles, and will be offset by a W17 upgrade package just around the corner.

That could still be the case, but team principal Toto Wolff has suddenly come out very firmly with the assertion that Mercedes "haven't got the money" - meaning cost cap allowance - to keep up with McLaren's upgrade rate.
"We left between 50 and 100 points on the table with reliability issues and that would have given us a little bit more of a gap than we have," Wolff also argued.
"Other than that, we're just continuing to execute what the plan was and what the financial realities mean for us."
Perhaps Mercedes always intended to make hay in the early part of the year - and, if that's the case, those dropped points Wolff references may indeed take on an extra significance.
Lando Norris has picked up a lot of stick over the past couple of years for some of the rougher edges of his racecraft, particularly when fighting Max Verstappen for titles.
But he was supreme on Sunday at Zandvoort, backing up a really strong season so far, which is arguably a step clear of most of his title-winning campaign.
The crowning moment of his Dutch GP victory was the move around the outside of championship leader Kimi Antonelli at the first corner.

"Definitely, he is now expressing a higher level of assertiveness, as he drives - the manoeuvre to pass Antonelli, I think is a really good demonstration of that," McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said.
"He is demonstrating more self-confidence, and this is interesting, and I quite like it.

"Self-confidence is sometimes not demonstrating by being the most aggressive. Sometimes you are self-confident, but you think, like, 'You know what? I'm not going to have a fight now, because I may lose in this fight. It's a very long race. See you at the end of the race'.
"It's confidence in your means, in your strength, that I quite like, which means that sometimes you are actually the one backing off, when the situation becomes too risky.

"We need to remember that in both of the last couple of races that he won, he didn't defend the pole position [on lap one]. He was actually second at the end of the first lap, but I did not hear or perceive any decay in his confidence, as to the fact that he was faster, he was just preparing his opportunity [rather] than cashing in on his self-confidence.
"Assertiveness and confidence are probably the two characteristics that he has improved the most from a non-technical, non-operational point of view."
Honda has a clear priority with new engine
Fernando Alonso's ninth-placed finish in the Dutch GP has shown the progress that both Aston Martin and Honda have made with their mid-season upgrades.

But despite its best result of the season so far and it no longer being adrift at the back, the team left Zandvoort well aware that there is a key area it needs to get on top of before it can start thinking of doing better: engine driveability.

A combination of the very complicated 2026 rules, plus Honda not being as on top of the combustion characteristics of the new power units as its rivals, has left it struggling to deliver an engine that does what the drivers want it to do at all times.
The biggest (but not only) problem is corner entry, where the engine can push on under braking, or trigger rejected downshifts, which then makes life super hard for the drivers.

Honda already had its Sakura dynos fired up to help find improvements over the weekend, with a first calibration tweak introduced for Dutch GP qualifying on Saturday. Further changes are coming for Monza.
More improvements there will be double good news. They will make life easier for the drivers but also help unlock more power.
That latter element is critical because, right now, the driveability headaches have left a big question mark over just how much of a step forward the latest Honda specification truly is.
Piastri 'a long way off' at too many races

Oscar Piastri remains a consistent threat to Norris over one lap: though the score is 4-13 over the year, in terms of the average gap they're still up there with the closest of F1's team-mate pairings.
But his grand prix was a particularly chastening experience, as evidenced by the half-minute gap to his team-mate at the finish.

"Lando has won the race by quite a lot so I think the car is in a good place, it's been quick the last two weekends, I think these two tracks suit the car well - it's just for whatever reason I've not been able to get the pace out of it," Piastri accepted.
"It's not the first race this year that that's been the case - some have been good, some have been very strong but there's been too many now that have been really a long way off."
Both Piastri and Stella did emphasise that it was really only one particular stint - the stint on the hards mid-race - that did the vast majority of the damage.
"We were not able to switch these tyres on. They stayed permanently in a regime of very-very low grip, which we didn't see in the first stint," Stella said.
Racing Bulls spoiled upgraded Alpine's debut
Alpine was overhauled by Racing Bulls for fifth place in the championship at the Hungaroring, and in performance terms had also slipped behind Audi to F1’s seventh-best car.
The team hoped its Zandvoort upgrade - only on Pierre Gasly’s car, with Franco Colapinto set to receive it at Monza - would change things.
And the evidence of the sprint race, where Gasly led the midfield and scored a point in eighth, certainly supported that the upgrade had changed that.
But Gasly’s chances of repeating that result in the grand prix were ruined by Arvid Lindblad’s Racing Bulls.
Lindblad played the team game by screwing over Gasly, as his race was already wrecked by picking up a drivethrough penalty for overtaking the Alpine driver under yellow flags.
He defended very hard against Gasly in the middle of the race, allowing Nico Hulkenberg's Audi and Yuki Tsunoda's Racing Bulls to slip through.
It limited Gasly to scoring one point in 10th place, but the Alpine driver suggested he'd take his revenge later in the year.

items.summaryEn: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur has explained what led to Lewis Hamilton's radio outbursts during a tough Dutch Grand Prix weekend. Ferrari failed to reach the podium for a second consecutive race, with Hamilton fourth and teammate Charles Leclerc fifth.
detailZh: 当刘易斯·汉密尔顿感觉自己像一只“小白鼠”时，法拉利实际上想做什么
这位七届世界冠军在上周日的F1荷兰大奖赛期间多次通过电台发泄情绪，法拉利已解释了其意图是什么
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
法拉利车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔澄清了在这个艰难的荷兰大奖赛周末中，是什么导致了刘易斯·汉密尔顿在电台上的情绪爆发。
车队连续第二场比赛未能登上领奖台，汉密尔顿获得第四名，队友夏尔·勒克莱尔（勒克莱尔）位列第五——与布达佩斯站正好相反——而法拉利在周日这场72圈的比赛中遭遇的关键时刻显然是什么已经很明显了。
第一次发生在比赛进行到一半时，汉密尔顿刚刚超越了迈凯伦车手奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里（皮亚斯特里）升到第五，并开始逼近速度慢得多的勒克莱尔。但由于赞德沃特赛道狭窄，这位七届世界冠军很难完成超车，因此不断请求车队下达车队指令，但指令始终没有到来，这让兰多·诺里斯（诺里斯）以及梅赛德斯的基米·安东内利（安东内利）和乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔）得以扩大他们前方领先的优势。
“你们真是浪费时间的好手，干得漂亮！”汉密尔顿讽刺地怼了一句。最终，当勒克莱尔在第43圈进行他的第二次进站时——比原计划晚了一圈——汉密尔顿拿到了第四名。
按照设想，这位英国车手应该在此后不久进站换上新轮胎，因为法拉利赛车周围的对手们都这么做了，但车队选择让汉密尔顿在场上多待了很久，这意味着他最终占据了领先位置。
但诺里斯（Norris）和安东内利（Antonelli）凭借更新的轮胎迅速逼近，到第53圈时他们之间的差距都在一秒以内。“你们是拿我当实验品吗？”汉密尔顿（Hamilton）打趣道，当迈凯伦和梅赛德斯分别在第54圈和第55圈超越他时，他几乎成了活靶子。
这位法拉利车手基本上被蒙在鼓里，不知道为什么他的第二段如此之长——30圈——直到第55圈因埃斯特班·奥孔（奥康）引发的虚拟安全车，这位41岁的车手才把硬胎换成了一套全新的软胎。
“我们不想在这个阶段告诉他策略，因为我们不想把它泄露给竞争对手，”瓦塞尔（Vasseur）说。“我们想让他留在赛道上直到最后，我认为那会是正确的决定。
“夏尔（Charles）本来应该进站的。我们多延了一圈，这有点混乱。我不担心这个。大家都会回到简报会上。他们会对这场比赛有清晰的了解。”
“Charles在某个阶段对轮胎配方的选择有点沮丧。我想大家当时对轮胎配方的选择都有点迷茫。Norris在第一次发车时[红旗之前]用的是中性胎，后来他换成了软胎。
“今天三种轮胎之间的差距非常微小。很难对策略有一个清晰的认识。有时候，我们必须改变策略或做出调整，因为我们在努力向其他人学习。对他们来说这有点令人沮丧。”
所以很明显，汉密尔顿赛后媒体会上讨论的焦点是什么，他在会上呼吁法拉利要有‘更好的执行力’。他以自己原来的车队梅赛德斯为榜样，提到银箭车队在比赛尾声迅速执行的车队指令——65圈时，冠军领跑者在VSC虚拟安全车下换上软胎后，Russell将第二位让给了Antonelli，而这位英国车手自己则继续用硬胎留在赛道上。
当汉密尔顿逼近他的前队友时，Russell起初告诉比赛工程师Marcus Dudley“我们丢掉了双领奖台”，但这位梅赛德斯车手守住了第三名，并在赛后表示这次交换位置是正确的决定。汉密尔顿认为，如果不是早些时候与Leclerc的那场混乱，他本有更好的机会在比赛尾声争夺领奖台，Vasseur也附和了这些评论，称“今天的执行力不太好”。
“你总可以在比赛之后说，要是跑到第46圈再进站就更好了，”这位法国人补充道。“情况是，当刘易斯（Lewis）追近查尔斯（Charles）时，我们原以为他会进站。
“当时我们安排了一个车手当僚机（处于赛车阴影位置）。我们让他多跑一圈。你不能要求他多跑一圈的同时还在直线上交换位置。这没那么容易。如果我现在回顾这场比赛，我可以看出差距所在。主要问题在于，我们没有告诉刘易斯我们原指望他坚持跑到最后。这不是关于推不推（速度）的问题。
这个结果使得法拉利落后领跑者梅赛德斯87分，领先第三名的迈凯伦75分，后者凭借诺里斯（Norris）从杆位出发连续夺冠，目前还剩下11轮比赛。
detailEn: What Ferrari actually meant to do when Lewis Hamilton felt like a "guinea pig"
The seven-time world champion had various radio outbursts during Sunday's F1 Dutch GP and Ferrari has explained what its intention was
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari
Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur has clarified what led to Lewis Hamilton’s radio outbursts during a tough Dutch Grand Prix weekend for the Formula 1 outfit.

The Scuderia finished off the podium for a second, consecutive race as Hamilton took fourth with team-mate Charles Leclerc in fifth – the reverse of Budapest – and it is clear what the defining moments were for Ferrari during Sunday’s 72-lap contest.

The first occurred midway through when Hamilton had just overtaken McLaren driver Oscar Piastri for fifth and started closing in on a much slower Leclerc. But due to the tight nature of Zandvoort, the seven-time world champion found it difficult to overtake and was therefore calling for team orders which didn’t arrive, allowing Lando Norris, plus Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, to increase their advantage up ahead.

“Great way of wasting time guys, good job!” snapped a sarcastic Hamilton, who eventually took fourth when Leclerc made his second pitstop on lap 43 – one tour after he was initially supposed to do so.

The assumption was that the Briton would come in for fresh tyres shortly afterwards, considering those around the Ferrari cars did the same, but the Scuderia opted to keep Hamilton out for much longer, which meant he eventually took the lead.

But Norris and Antonelli rapidly closed in on fresher tyres, and by lap 53 they were all within a second of each other. “Are you using me as a guinea pig?” quipped Hamilton, who was practically a sitting duck as the McLaren and Mercedes respectively overtook him on laps 54 and 55.

The Ferrari driver was essentially left in the dark as to why his second stint was so long - 30 laps - and it required a lap 55 virtual safety car caused by Esteban Ocon for the 41-year-old to ditch his hard tyres for a fresh set of softs.

“We didn't want to tell him the strategy at this stage because we didn't want to disclose it to the competitors,” said Vasseur. “We wanted to keep him on track until the end, I think it would have been the right call.
“Charles was supposed to pit. We extended one lap and it was a kind of confusion. I'm not worried about this. Everybody will be back in the briefing. They will have a clear picture about the race.

“Charles was a bit frustrated at one stage about the compound. I think everybody was a bit lost about the compound. Norris started with mediums on the first start [before the red flag], then he moved to softs.

“The difference between the three compounds was very marginal today. It was difficult to have a clear picture on the strategy. Sometimes, we have to change the strategy or adapt, because we are trying to learn from the others. For them it's a bit frustrating.”

So it’s obvious what dominated discussions in Hamilton’s post-race media session, during which he called for Ferrari to have ‘better execution’. He cited his former team Mercedes as inspiration, considering the late team orders the Silver Arrows quickly deployed as Russell handed second to Antonelli on lap 65 after the championship leader took softs under the VSC, while the Briton stayed out on hards.

Russell initially told race engineer Marcus Dudley that “we’ve lost a double podium” as Hamilton closed in on his former team-mate, but the Mercedes driver held on for third and post-race said the swap was the correct decision. Had it not been for the earlier fiasco with Leclerc, Hamilton reckons he’d have had a better shot at claiming a late podium and Vasseur echoed those comments, claiming “the execution today was not that good”.
“You can always say after the race that it would have been better to do it on lap 46,” the Frenchman added. “The story is that, when Lewis came back on Charles, we were expecting him to pit.

“Then we had someone in the shadow of the car. We asked him to do one lap more. You can't ask him to do one lap more and to swap positions in the straight line. It's not so easy. If I have a look at the race now, I can see the difference. The main issue is that we didn't tell Lewis that we were expecting him to go to the end. It was not a matter of pushing.”
The result leaves Ferrari 87 points behind leader Mercedes and 75 ahead of third-placed McLaren, which has taken consecutive wins from pole via Norris, with 11 rounds remaining.

items.titleZh: 加斯利警告小红牛：他们毁了我们的比赛，我不会忘记
items.summaryZh: 阿尔派车手皮埃尔·加斯利将他在荷兰大奖赛正赛的失望成绩归咎于小红牛车队的战术，两队正在车队积分榜上激烈竞争。他在赞德福特赛道表现出色，冲刺赛排位第八并第八名完赛，但正赛仅从第11位发车。

items.originalTitle: 加斯利警告Racing Bulls：他们毁了我们的比赛，我不会忘记

He impressed at Zandvoort by qualifying and finishing eighth in the sprint, but started the main race only 11th.
detailZh: 皮埃尔·加斯利对小红牛发出的警告：‘他们毁了我们的比赛，我不会忘记这件事’
皮埃尔·加斯利对小红牛在赞德福特使用的战术感到沮丧，并打算复仇
阿尔派车队的一级方程式车手皮埃尔·加斯利将自己在荷兰大奖赛上不尽如人意的成绩归咎于小红牛车队在周日正赛中的车队战术，目前两队在车队总冠军积分榜上正展开激烈争夺。
加斯利在赞德福特状态不错，他在冲刺赛中排位第八、并以第八名完赛——换句话说，是“除顶尖车队之外的最佳”——尽管他在正赛的发车区只排在第11位。
然而，一个强劲的发车让这位前小红牛（小红牛）车手迅速爬升到第八位——但这只是在他第一次进站之前，那次进站让他落到了阿尔维德·林德布拉德（Arvid Lindblad）身后，后者因在黄旗状态下违规被处以通过维修区处罚（drive-through penalty），已经退出了积分争夺。
加斯利被林德布拉德（Arvid Lindblad）挡了七圈，直到他尝试在11号弯从外线超越，但发生了锁死，随即被尼科·霍肯伯格（霍肯伯格）超越，此时角田裕毅（角田裕毅）也紧跟在他身后。
霍肯伯格（霍肯伯格）很快就解决了林德布拉德（Arvid Lindblad），但加斯利仍然做不到，而角田裕毅（角田裕毅）则在7号弯漂亮地超越了阿尔派，这个动作是他在3号弯的倾斜弯道中提前铺垫完成的。
林德布拉德（Arvid Lindblad）毫不意外地轻松让自己的小红牛（小红牛）队友通过，但加斯利依然苦苦挣扎。总体而言，这位法国车手总共花了整整17圈才完成超越。
皮埃尔·加斯利（阿尔派车队）位于小红牛车队的角田裕毅身后。
让他的问题雪上加霜的是，加斯利在第二次进站后发现自己落在了角田裕毅身后，并且又花了10圈才找到办法超越这位前队友。
“VCARB在比赛的中段毁掉了我们的比赛，为车队锦标赛打了一场团队牌，而且打得很好，”加斯利惋惜道。“我是说，这让我丢掉了一个位置，输给了尼科和角田，还不知道损失了多少秒的比赛时间。恭喜他们，我等不及再和他们比了。”
小红牛车队的策略对这支位于法恩扎的车队本身没有任何影响——他们未能得分，因为角田裕毅和林德布拉德分别以第11和第12名完赛——但肯定让加斯利付出了第九名的代价。他最终落后阿隆索一秒冲线，此前在跟在林德布拉德身后时，尽管用的是新轮胎，他还是损失了四秒；随后角田裕毅这块绊脚石又阻止了这位阿尔派车手尽快追上采用一停策略的阿斯顿·马丁。
“这确实让人恼火，但这就是赞德沃特，”加斯利补充道。“这里真的很难超车，而接下来的赛道情况会有所改变。好消息是我的记性很好，所以我会确保我们在赛季结束时能够笑到最后。”
然而，当Motorsport.com网站把加斯利的这番话转述给林德布拉德时，他显得毫不在意：“我不知道。嗯，这算是个不错的故事。总之，我顾全了车队的大局。我不知道。”
“如果他的记性很好，那挺好。总之，每个周末我们都会全力以赴地拼争。我在力所能及的地方尽力帮助了车队。实际情况是，我的比赛当时已经没什么指望了，所以我做了自己能做的来帮助车队。”
这两支车队正在为车队锦标赛第五名展开激烈争夺，小红牛目前积66分，而阿尔派已升至63分。
detailEn: Pierre Gasly’s warning to Racing Bulls: ‘They ruined our race, and I won’t forget it’
Pierre Gasly was dismayed by Racing Bulls’ tactics at Zandvoort and intends to take revenge
Alpine Formula 1 driver Pierre Gasly has blamed his underwhelming Dutch Grand Prix result on Racing Bulls’ team tactics in Sunday’s race, amid their tight battle in the constructors’ championship.
Gasly was on form in Zandvoort, where he qualified and finished eighth in the sprint – ‘best of the rest’, in other words – although he took just 11th on the grid for the main race.

A strong start, however, meant the former Racing Bulls racer swiftly climbed to eighth – but that was until his first pitstop dropped him behind Arvid Lindblad, whose drive-through penalty for a yellow-flag infringement had taken him out of contention for points.
Gasly spent seven laps stuck behind Lindblad until he attempted an overtake around the outside of Turn 11, but locked up and was passed by Nico Hulkenberg, with Yuki Tsunoda now tailing him.
Hulkenberg made short work of Lindblad, but Gasly still couldn’t and Tsunoda impressively overtook the Alpine into Turn 7, a move he set up in the banked Turn 3 curve.
While Lindblad unsurprisingly made it easy for his Racing Bulls team-mate to go through, Gasly kept struggling. Overall, it took a whopping 17 laps in total for the Frenchman to get by.
Pierre Gasly, Alpine, behind Yuki Tsunoda, Racing Bulls
To compound his issues, Gasly found himself behind Tsunoda after his second pitstop and required another 10 laps to find a way past his former team-mate.

“VCARB ruined our race in the middle part of the race, played a team game for the championship and did it well,” Gasly lamented. “I mean, it just made me lose a position to Nico and Tsunoda and I don't know how many seconds of race time. Congrats to them, and I can't wait to race them.”

The Racing Bulls strategy had no impact on the Faenza-based team, which failed to score points as Tsunoda and Lindblad finished 11th and 12th, but most certainly cost Gasly ninth place. He finished one second behind Fernando Alonso after losing four seconds to the Spaniard – despite new tyres – when he was behind Lindblad; then the Tsunoda stumbling block prevented the Alpine driver from catching the Aston Martin, which was one-stopping, as quickly as he could have.

“It's just annoying, but it's Zandvoort,” Gasly added. “Can't really overtake, and this is going to change in the coming tracks. And good thing is I have a good memory, so I'm going to make sure we smile at the end of the year.”
Yet, when Motorsport.com put Gasly’s comments to him, Lindblad was unfazed: “I don't know. Yeah, that's a nice story. In the end, yeah, I played the team game. I don’t know.

“If he has a good memory, then fine. In the end, we all fight as hard as we can every weekend. I tried to help the team where I could. The reality was, my race, I wasn't really in it anymore, so yeah, I did what I could to help the team.”
The two outfits are locked in a close fight for fifth place in the constructors’ championship, with Racing Bulls on 66 points and Alpine now up to 63.

items.titleZh: F1车迷需要更少的冲刺赛，而非更多
items.summaryZh: 荷兰大奖赛周六阿姆斯特丹铁路故障可能导致数千车迷错过冲刺赛，但作者认为这或许是好事，并批评冲刺赛数量过多的趋势。
items.originalTitle: F1车迷需要更少的冲刺赛，而非更多
items.summaryEn: Technical problems on Amsterdam's train network during Dutch Grand Prix weekend risked leaving thousands of fans unable to attend the sprint, but the author argues this may be a blessing because F1 needs fewer sprint races rather than more.
detailZh: 在荷兰大奖赛周末的周六早上，阿姆斯特丹周边的铁路网络遭遇了大规模的技术故障，数千名车迷有可能因此错过冲刺赛。
当这24圈毫无波澜的比赛展开时，坐在（或者说站着）拥挤的公共交通工具上，读一篇那种在Kindle Unlimited服务上泛滥成灾的、由AI生成的低劣同人垃圾小说，恐怕都比在看台上硬塑料长椅上占个位置要舒服。这是给那些把冲刺赛安排在几乎不可能超车的场地（除了轮胎性能这一看不见的玄机之外）的人上的一堂愚蠢课。'拿好我的赫托赫·扬啤酒！诺里斯的后胎在衰减！'——从来没有人说过这种话。
社交媒体在过去几年里一直是浪费时间的毒瘤，但这次它多少恢复了一点往日那种偶尔有趣的模样，用户们发布了诸如'这场比赛本来可以是一封电子邮件……'之类的妙语。人们确实会觉得，任何真正渴望看到车手们列队绕场的人，大可以在周日的午间如愿，届时他们会站在平板卡车上向人群挥手。如果那样还不满足，也可以再让他们坐进乐高赛车里。
支持冲刺赛周末的一个长期论点是，练习时间较少往往会让比赛结果更难预测，因为车队没有足够的时间去精细调校赛车。这大体上是对的。另一个支持的理由是，通常占据整个周末的练习赛对观众来说本质上就很枯燥，因为没有任何真正的故事线——只有赛车按着观众看不见的计划在赛道上绕圈。这一点也很难反驳——但那和一场伪装成赛车比赛的高速巡游之间，真的有本质区别吗？
同样无可争辩的是商业现实：赛事推广方喜欢冲刺赛周末，因为冲刺赛能卖出更多门票——这也是为什么F1计划在下赛季把冲刺赛数量翻倍至12场。再说一次，这没问题——但比赛质量必须更好，否则冲刺赛周末就应该安排在那些具备超车条件的赛道上，而不是通过某种晦涩的恩惠制度来运作——把冲刺赛当作对推广方的一种激励或摸摸头的奖励。
勒克莱尔在赞德沃特的冲刺赛中完成了一项罕见壮举——超越了一辆别的车。
可以理解赞德沃特被给了一点甜头，以便在它的最后一场比赛里最大化周末门票销售，毕竟扬·拉默斯和他的团队在没有国家支持的情况下，以私营企业的形式为复兴荷兰大奖赛投入了大量精力。但偏偏是新加坡将承办下一场冲刺赛，原因只有商业权益持有者自己知道。
是时候承认冲刺赛赛制并不适合所有场地了。诚然，赞德沃特即将进入历史，但赛历上仍有许多赛道只有一个可行的超车区域，追赶的赛车必须比前车快半秒才能完成超越。再叠加大多数车手使用相同轮胎的情况，一场列队行进式的比赛就在所难免。
遗憾的是，一级方程式（F1）本身似乎持相反的观点——即冲刺赛赛制已是最终成品，无需再进行迭代改进。该赛制最初在2021年的三场比赛中进行评估时，形式是周五举行排位赛，其成绩决定周六冲刺赛的发车顺序，而冲刺赛的结果又决定了大奖赛的正赛发车顺序。
既然一级方程式（F1）已经足够聪明，能够通过迭代改进摆脱最初的缺陷，那么继续这一过程、进一步审视这一赛制，难道不也是明智之举吗
很快人们就发现，这样做只不过是按速度顺序重新排列了发车顺序，因此赛制演变成现在的形式——排位赛和 Parking（ Parking）封闭检录期分开进行，使冲刺赛实际上与大奖赛相互独立。至少它不再充当主赛事的破坏者了。
鉴于一级方程式（F1）已经足够聪明，能够通过迭代改进摆脱最初的缺陷，那么考虑到上述明显的缺陷，继续这一过程并进一步审视这一赛制，难道不也是明智之举吗？由于冲刺赛从根本上乏味无趣，车手和车迷们普遍对其持批评态度。

显然，如今“车迷”这个词承载了很多含义，因为F1车迷群体的庞大意味着它涵盖了广泛的人口结构。这使得F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利可以轻松地摆摆手说，大多数车迷并不在乎这些事情，却没有任何有意义的数据来支持他的说法。就在上周末，多梅尼卡利在接受《电讯报》采访时又一次滑入了“意外帕特里奇”（Accidental Partridge，指无意中说出滑稽言论）的领域，他在谈到2026年技术规则时评论道：“有些铁杆车迷会在一个F1比赛周末谈论地面效应（clipping，指气流下压力相关现象），但也会有许多人认为夹子（clip）是你别在头发上的东西。”
要不要冲刺赛，这是一个问题
detailEn: A plague of technical problems beset the train network out of Amsterdam on the Saturday morning of the Dutch Grand Prix weekend, raising the possibility that thousands of fans might miss the sprint race.

Sitting, or indeed standing, on a crowded vessel of public transport reading one of those wretched pieces of AI-generated slash-fiction slop which bedevil the Kindle Unlimited service would probably have been preferable to occupying a hard plastic bench in the bleachers as the 24 processional laps unfolded. It was an object lesson in the folly of holding these sprint events at venues where overtaking is unlikely, save for the invisible machinations of tyre performance. Hold my Hertog Jan! Norris's rear tyres are degrading! – said no one, ever.

Social media, a toxic waste of time these past couple of years, assumed some semblance of its former sporadically amusing self as users posted wit such as "This race could have been an e-mail…"Certainly one felt that anyone with a burning desire to see the drivers parading around in a line could do so on Sunday lunchtime when they wave at the crowd from the back of a flatbed truck. Failing that, they could put them in Lego cars again.

The long-standing argument in favour of sprint weekends is that having less practice time tends to lead to less predictable outcomes, since the teams have less time to finesse their set-ups. This, more or less, is true. Another point in favour is that practice sessions such as usually populate a weekend are inherently tedious for the audience, since there is no real narrative – just cars circulating a track to an unseen plan. Also difficult to dispute – but is there really such a difference between that and a high-speed procession masquerading as a motor race?

Also inarguable is the commercial reality that race promoters love sprint weekends because they sell more tickets - which is why F1 plans to double the number to 12 next season. Again, fine – but the racing needs to be better, or the sprint weekends should be distributed around those circuits where overtaking is possible, rather than operating via some abstruse grace and favour system where promoters get a sprint as an incentive or a pat on the head.
Leclerc achieved a rarity in the Zandvoort sprint - overtaking another car

One can understand Zandvoort being handed a little something to maximise weekend ticket sales for its final event, given the energy Jan Lammers and his team have invested in bringing the Dutch GP back to life as a private enterprise without state backing. But Singapore, of all places, will host the next sprint race, for reasons known only to the commercial rights holder.

It's time to accept that the sprint format isn't suitable for all venues. Granted, Zandvoort is now heading into the vault of history, but there are plenty of other tracks still on the calendar with only one practicable overtaking zone requiring the chasing car to be half a second quicker than the chased. Combine that with most of the field running the same tyre and a procession is inevitable.

Sadly, F1 itself seems to take the contrasting view – that the sprint format is the finished product with no further need for iterative development. When first evaluated, over three events in 2021, the format was a qualifying session on Friday which set the grid for Saturday's sprint race, the results of which in term determined the grid for the grand prix.
F1 was smart enough to iterate away from the initial flaws, would it not also be wise to continue that process and interrogate the format further

What quickly became obvious was that all this did was reset the grid in pace order, hence the evolution into the present format with separate qualifying sessions and parc ferme periods so the sprint in effect lives separately from the grand prix. At least it no longer functions as a spoiler for the main event.

Given that F1 was smart enough to iterate away from the initial flaws, would it not also be wise to continue that process and interrogate the format further, given the obvious shortcomings outlined above? The sprint races remain widely derided by drivers and fans, given their fundamentally uneventful nature.

Obviously the word "fans" does a lot of heavy lifting these days, since the size of F1's fanbase means it incorporates a broad demographic spectrum. This enables F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali to wave his hands and say airily, with no meaningful data to back up his contention, that most fans don't care about such things. Only last weekend, for instance, Domenicali once again sailed into Accidental Partridge territory in an interview with De Telegraaf where he opined, apropos the 2026 tech regulations, "There are die-hard fans who talk about clipping during a Formula 1 weekend, but there will also be many who think a clip is something you put in your hair."
To sprint or not to sprint, that is the question

Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonlli will start at the back of the grid in his Italian Grand Prix home race as Mercedes has decided on a full power unit change

Mercedes has officially decided its Formula 1 world championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start from the back of the grid at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix after it decided to give him a new power unit, exceeding his allowance for the year.

Drivers are allowed to use up to four power units for the season, but Mercedes' reliability woes over the first half of the campaign meant it has always been a question of when, not if, its drivers were going to exceed that allowance and take a grid penalty.
Antonelli is currently already at the limit with his V6 and exhaust system, while Russell has no more room for either a combustion engine or turbocharger.

Antonelli had been in line for a grid drop at his home race in Monza in two weeks' time, and Mercedes has now officially confirmed it will change the title favourite's engine. The 19-year-old is set for a full power unit switch, which sets him up for a back-of-the-grid start.
"With Kimi we are taking the full thing," Wolff confirmed, dismissing the notion that Mercedes could have been tempted to take into account Monza being Antonelli's home race.

"In theory, our calculations say that that's the best track to take it. Obviously, our algorithms don't take nationality into consideration. But we are here to fight for a championship and not get the most PR. So, that's what we are going to do."
Russell is also set for grid drop down the line, though the Brackley team hasn't decided yet where the Briton will swap power units yet.

Russell only took his fourth power unit at the recent Hungarian Grand Prix, the final race before the summer break. That gives him more flexibility on mileage, though the team could still opt to add a fifth power unit to his pool of components at any time.
"With George, the discussions are ongoing about where to take it," Wolff said.

The next suitable opportunity after Monza could be Baku's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which emphasises power unit performance and top speed while providing some overtaking opportunities to offset a grid drop.

items.originalTitle: 斯特罗尔要求处罚：贝尔曼和博尔托莱托闯红灯出站
items.summaryEn: During the Dutch Grand Prix, Lance Stroll noticed Oliver Bearman and Gabriel Bortoleto passing a red light at the pit lane exit and urged race control to penalise them, but the stewards only issued reprimands to the two drivers.
detailZh: 兰斯·斯特罗尔敦促赛事控制中心处罚他的两位对手，因为他们在荷兰大奖赛期间红灯亮起时驶离了维修区。
事件发生在马克斯·维斯塔潘撞车导致比赛暂停后，车阵重新起步离开维修区时。
当车阵开始离开维修区时，维修区出口的指示灯是绿色的。然而在费尔南多·阿隆索经过信号灯后，信号变为闪烁的红灯。
奥利弗·贝尔曼和加布里埃尔·博尔托莱托都驶过了闪烁的红灯。两人均未确认维修区出口已关闭，并继续前往发车格，尽管贝尔曼在到达前遭遇了动力单元故障。
跟在两人后面的斯特罗尔注意到信号灯已变化，并提醒他的比赛工程师加里·甘农：
信号变为绿色，斯特罗尔驶离维修区出口。
他多次呼吁对闯红灯的车手进行处罚。斯特罗尔正确指出，F1的处罚指南规定，在比赛中驶过维修区出口红灯的车手应被处以10秒停车处罚：
“所以所有闯红灯的人都应该受罚。”
“明白，我们会报告。那么后面的车阵……”
“……后面的车阵在九号弯，你可以开始建立胎温。好好推来建立胎温。”
斯特罗尔似乎认为，闯红灯的车手远不止他正前方的两位：
“很明显所有人都闯了红灯，那么他们都应该受罚。”
“一开始是绿灯，然后变红了，我们正在检查谁闯了红灯并尽快报告。绝对，兰斯。”
这位阿斯顿·马丁车手在编队圈继续施压，即使他的比赛工程师试图提醒他前方贝尔曼停车：
“‘贝尔曼在10-11号弯之间很慢。前方黄旗，贝尔曼停车。贝尔曼停在10-11号弯之间。注意贝尔曼……’”
“兰斯，我们已经报告了，我们报告了。现在让我们集中精力绕到发车格，好吗？我们已经报告了，他们会处理的。”
然而，赛事干事选择只对两人进行训诫，指出事件发生在比赛重新开始之前，且两人均未获得优势。
他们指出：“当车手在比赛暂停后重新起步时接近维修区出口加入赛道时，维修区出口的灯变红了。此类违规行为如果发生在比赛中，通常需要非常严厉的处罚，因为车手有义务始终遵守灯光信号。然而，在本案中，违规行为并非发生在比赛进行期间，而是在重新起步前的准备阶段，尽管根据第B5.15.2g条，比赛在技术上已经恢复。”
“此外，赛事干事承认，既未获得任何优势，也未造成任何潜在危险或不安全的情况。因此，考虑到减轻处罚的情节和这一独特情况，对车手进行训诫被认为是适当的。”
detailEn: Lance Stroll urged race control to penalise two of his rivals for leaving the pit lane while a red light was shown during the Dutch Grand Prix.
The incident occured as the field left the pits when the race resumed following the stoppage caused by Max Verstappen’s crash.
The pit lane exit lights were green as the field began to leave the pits. However after Fernando Alonso passed by the signal changed to a flashing red light.

Oliver Bearman and Gabriel Bortoleto both drove past the flashing red light. Neither acknowledged the pit lane exit had been closed and continued to the grid, though Bearman suffered a power unit failure before he got there.
Stroll, who was following the pair, noticed the light had changed and alerted his race engineer Gary Gannon:
The signal changes to green and Stroll leaves the pit exit

He repeatedly called for the drivers who had passed the red signal to be penalised. Stroll correctly noted that Formula 1’s penalty guidelines state drivers who pass a red light at the pit lane exit during a race should receive 10-second stop-and-go penalties:
So everybody that went under a red should get a penalty.
Understood, we’ll report it. So the back of the pack…
…the back of the pack is in nine, so you can build temp. Good pushing to build temp
Stroll appeared to be under the impression that many more drivers than just the two immediately in front of him had driven past the red signal:
It’s clear that everyone went under red, then they all should get a penalty.
It started out green and then it went red and we’re checking who went through red and reporting it ASAP. Absolutely Lance.
The Aston Martin driver continued to press his case on the formation lap, even when his race engineer was trying to warn him about Bearman’s stoppage ahead:
‘Bearman is slow between 10-11. Yellow ahead for Bearman stopped. Bearman stopped between 10-11. Watch for Bearman…
Lance, we’ve reported it, we reported it. Now let’s get focused getting around to the grid, okay? We’ve reported and they will action it.
However the stewards chose instead to only reprimand the pair, pointing out that the incident occured before the race resumption and neither had gained an advantage.

“The pit exit light turned red when the driver was approaching the pit exit to join the track for the re-start of the race after a suspension,” they noted. “Such an infringement happening during the race normally requires a very significant penalty as the drivers are obliged to obey light signals at all times. However, in this case the infringement did not happen during a live race, but rather on the build-up before the re-start, although the race had technically already resumed in accordance with Article B5.15.2g.

“In addition to that, the stewards acknowledge that neither any advantage was gained nor any potentially dangerous or unsafe situation was created. Therefore a reprimand to the driver is deemed appropriate given the mitigating circumstances and the unique scenario.”

赛事干事指出事件发生在比赛重新开始前，两人未获得优势，因此仅给予训诫。
keyPointsEn: The incident occurred before the restart following the stoppage caused by Max Verstappen's crash, when the pit exit light changed from green to flashing red.
Stroll believed all drivers who passed the red light should be penalised, noting that F1 penalty guidelines state a 10-second stop-and-go penalty.
The stewards noted the incident happened before the race resumed and neither driver gained an advantage, so they only issued reprimands.

detailZh: 昨晚睡得最差的人：奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里
奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里不可能忘了怎么赛车——然而短短一年时间，他在一级方程式中的处境已经发生了翻天覆地的变化
2025年8月31日，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在赞德沃特赢得了荷兰大奖赛，而兰多·诺里斯则因漏油退赛。面对那份苦涩的失望，诺里斯说他只想"买个汉堡回家"。当时他在车手锦标赛积分榜上落后皮亚斯特里34分，而我当天的赛后报道标题就在问：赞德沃特这一站是否实际上已经决定了年度冠军的归属。
如今回头看，那个世界几乎像是一个超现实的平行宇宙。在那个宇宙里，皮亚斯特里即将成为一级方程式世界冠军；诺里斯却不知怎么被贴上了标签——一个每当关键时刻来临总是差一口气的天才；基米·安东内利只有64分，而乔治·拉塞尔有184分。我愿意坦率承认，我自己当时也是那些暗自嘀咕托托·沃尔夫是否终究看走了眼这位意大利小将的人之一。
如今，诺里斯已经成为了世界冠军，就连尼科·罗斯伯格也认为安东内尔 有点像是下一个埃尔顿·塞纳，而如果那些最乐观的人真的相信迈凯伦还能在2026年的冠军争夺中有一席之地，那他们心里想的恐怕也只有诺里斯一个人。
在短短12个月里，皮亚斯特里从一个“未来冠军”变成了越来越像是迈凯伦非官方二号车手的人。他的经纪人马克·韦伯曾被许多人视为这位澳大利亚车手通往世界冠军之路上的重要拼图，如今似乎也沦为了“皮亚斯特里团队”中的边缘人物。而且，随着这位25岁车手在赞德沃特落后诺里斯32秒完赛，目前在积分榜上又落后他55分，你可能会觉得这已经说明了一切。数字通常不会说谎。
听到安德烈亚·斯特拉盛赞诺里斯在抓地力低、轮胎硬的条件下充分发挥了他非凡的天赋，而对皮亚斯特里，斯特拉却接着说，这位澳大利亚人必须用2026年的迈凯伦做出违背自己驾驶直觉的操作，才能勉强接近发挥出赛车的全部潜力——这对皮亚斯特里来说一定很不好受。
倒不是说斯特拉做错了什么。这位前法拉利车手出身的人可能是一级方程式里最有外交手腕的车队领队。他把文字游戏玩得炉火纯青，绝不会让哪怕最细微的印象流露出来，让人觉得他把一位车手当一号、另一位当二号。
但一年过去了，很多一直在Reddit等平台上坚持认为诺里斯才是迈凯伦暗中偏爱的车手——尤其是在首席执行官扎克·布朗眼中——的车迷现在觉得自己得到了印证。就好像诺里斯是长子，而皮亚斯特里'只不过'是他们始终没能学会同样去疼爱的养子。
皮亚斯特里不太可能在短短12个月里就忘了怎么驾驶赛车。但他输掉2025年总冠军的原因之一，或许是在赞德沃特之后，那种让他免于从进攻模式切换到保分模式的随和沉稳突然消失了。而且，2026年这一代一级方程式赛车似乎也不是他最喜欢玩的那种'玩具'。
"很遗憾，这不是第一场节奏就是上不来的比赛，"皮亚斯特里在赛后接受电视采访区（TV pen）采访时叹着气，试图解释自己第六名的成绩。几米之外，诺里斯独自一人坐在国际汽联的新闻发布会上，微笑着说出这样的话："我确实正在消除自己在赛道上的弱点，而且我已经没有太多弱点了。"
当皮亚斯特里从雷诺转投迈凯伦——这是一桩合同条款错综复杂、充满暗箱操作色彩的一级方程式近年最具争议的转会之一——他带着天才少年的美誉而来。在进入一级方程式之前，他几乎赢得了所有能赢的冠军；在与诺里斯搭档度过一个稳健但算不上惊艳的新秀赛季后，2025年的大部分时间里，他似乎都在证明外界的每一分炒作都是物有所值。
当诺里斯公开谈论自己的情绪和弱点时——许多人将此解读为他盔甲上一道非常人性化的裂痕——皮亚斯特里却话不多。他只是不断地赢得比赛。冷血、沉着冷静，没有多余的表演。
但2026年的F1已经与室内卡丁车场上业余车手所熟悉的那种赛车相去甚远——在那里，归根结底，胆子最大的人只要比所有人都更快、更干净地过弯并且避免麻烦，就能获胜。新的F1更像一盘棋。胆量依然重要，但巧妙地调配能量输出等复杂参数、并从轮胎中榨取巅峰性能，已经成为压倒一切的关键。
或者换一种说法：曾几何时，仅凭成为驾驶赛车最快的人就能让你成为世界冠军。在一个整体水准可能达到历史最高的车手中，仅凭这一点已经远远不够了。
把整个2026年的车手阵容都放回2025年的赛车上，将是一项非常有趣的实验。皮亚斯特里会重新开始获胜吗？刘易斯·汉密尔顿还会在法拉利挣扎吗？归根结底，这无关紧要。F1世界冠军是在现实世界中赢得的。平行宇宙只存在于Reddit上。不过对车迷来说，沉浸其中也可以是极大的乐趣。
皮亚斯特里这样的车手和安东内利这样的车手是有区别的。安东内利在蒙扎的第一场一级方程式练习赛上就如闪电般横空出世。所有人都看得出来，这孩子非同凡响。他是个天生的天才，生来就拥有正确的直觉。
皮亚斯特里看起来更像是那种需要多一点时间来适应新环境，之后才能真正大放异彩的车手。
这并不是说他天生就缺乏天赋。如果一两年后，头条新闻讲述的是一个完全不同的故事，我丝毫不会感到意外。汉密尔顿已经证明，真正伟大的车手永远不应该被轻易否定。
也许下次当皮亚斯特里因为想得太多而彻夜难眠时，他可以抓住这个榜样来给自己打气……
detailEn: Who slept worst last night: Oscar Piastri
Oscar Piastri can't have forgotten how to race – and yet his standing in Formula 1 has changed dramatically in the space of just one year

On 31 August 2025, Oscar Piastri won the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, while Lando Norris retired with an oil leak. Faced with that bitter disappointment, Norris said all he wanted to do was "grab a burger and go home". He was 34 points behind Piastri in the championship, and my own race report that day carried a headline asking whether Zandvoort had effectively decided the title.

Looking back now, that world almost feels like some surreal parallel universe. One in which Piastri was on the verge of becoming a Formula 1 world champion; Norris had somehow been labelled the perennial talent who, when push came to shove, could never quite get the job done; Kimi Antonelli had 64 points to George Russell's 184. I will readily admit that I, too, was among those quietly wondering whether Toto Wolff might just have got it wrong with the young Italian after all.

Now, Norris is the world champion, even Nico Rosberg regards Antonelli as something akin to the next Ayrton Senna, and if the most bullish optimists genuinely believe McLaren can still have a say in the 2026 title fight, they are probably thinking of Norris alone.

In the space of 12 months, Piastri has gone from champion-in-the-making to what increasingly feels like McLaren's unofficial number two. His manager Mark Webber, whom many once regarded as an important piece of the puzzle in the Australian's path to the world championship, has seemingly been reduced to a peripheral figure in Team Piastri. And with the 25-year-old finishing 32 seconds behind Norris at Zandvoort and now trailing him by 55 points in the championship, you might think that says everything. Numbers usually don't lie.

It must hurt Piastri to hear Andrea Stella wax lyrical about Norris fully exploiting his exceptional talent when grip is low and tyres are hard. And then, in the same breath, explain that Piastri has to do things with the 2026 McLaren that go against his natural driving instincts simply to get anywhere near extracting the car's full potential.

Not that Stella is doing anything wrong. The former Ferrari man is probably the most diplomatic team principal in Formula 1. He plays the game of words so skillfully that he would never allow even the faintest impression to emerge that he regards one of his drivers as number one and the other as number two.

But a year on, plenty of those fans who have always insisted on Reddit and elsewhere that Norris was McLaren's secret favourite all along – particularly in the eyes of CEO Zak Brown – now feel vindicated. As if Norris were the first-born son, while Piastri was 'merely' the adopted child they never quite learned to love in the same way.

It seems unlikely that Piastri has forgotten how to race a car in the space of 12 months. But perhaps one of the reasons he lost the 2025 championship was that, after Zandvoort, the easy-going composure that might have protected him from switching from attack mode to points-management mode in response to his championship lead suddenly disappeared. And because the 2026 generation of Formula 1 cars does not appear to be the kind of toy he most enjoys playing with.

"Unfortunately it's not the first race where the pace just hasn't been there," Piastri sighed after the race as he tried to explain his sixth-place finish in the TV pen. A few metres away, Norris sat all by himself in the FIA press conference, smiling and saying things like: "I'm certainly eliminating my weaknesses on track, and I don't have so many."

When Piastri moved from Renault to McLaren in one of the more controversial transfers in recent Formula 1 history – a contractually convoluted cloak-and-dagger affair – he arrived with the reputation of a potential prodigy. Before reaching Formula 1, he had won (almost) everything there was to win, and after a solid, if not spectacular, rookie season alongside Norris, he spent much of 2025 appearing to justify every ounce of the hype.

While Norris spoke openly about his emotions and weaknesses – something many interpreted as a very human crack in his armour – Piastri did not say much. He simply won motor races. Cold-blooded, unflappable, stripped of unnecessary theatrics.

But Formula 1 in 2026 has moved a long way from the version of motor racing familiar to amateur racers at indoor kart tracks, where ultimately the guy with the biggest balls wins by driving through the corners faster and cleaner than everyone else while staying out of trouble. The new Formula 1 is more like a game of chess. Having the biggest balls still matters, but intelligently juggling complex parameters such as energy deployment and extracting peak performance from the tyres has taken on overriding importance.

Or, to put it another way: there was a time when being the fastest man at driving a racing car could make you world champion. In a field whose overall standard is probably higher than ever before, that alone is no longer remotely enough.

It would make for a fascinating experiment to put the entire 2026 grid back into the 2025 cars. Would Piastri start winning again? Would Lewis Hamilton still struggle with the Ferrari? Ultimately, it is irrelevant. Formula 1 world championships are won in the real world. Parallel universes exist only on Reddit. And, for fans, it can be great fun to lose yourself in them.

There is a difference between the Piastris of this world and the Antonellis. Antonelli burst onto the scene like a bolt of lightning in his very first Formula 1 practice session at Monza. Everyone could see that this kid was something special. A natural talent, born with the right instincts.
Piastri seems more like the kind of racing driver who needs a little more time to adapt to new circumstances before he can truly flourish.

That is not to suggest that he is somehow inherently less gifted. It would not surprise me in the slightest if, in a year or two, the headlines were telling a very different story again. Hamilton has proven that the genuinely great drivers should never be written off.
Perhaps that is an example Piastri can cling to the next time all that overthinking keeps him awake at night...

detailZh: 利亚姆·劳森终于迎来了他的“本可以怎样”时刻
利亚姆·劳森在红牛的第三场比赛正是红牛当初希望从利亚姆·劳森身上看到的表现。排位赛表现出色，紧紧跟在马克斯·维斯塔潘身后。比赛中没有犯大错，节奏强劲，还拿到了积分。他终于证明了自己配得上那个席位……
只不过，他在红牛的第三场比赛并不是2025年4月的铃鹿，而是大约17个月之后的赞德沃特。
那么，我们该如何解读劳森的这个周末呢？它到底又证明了什么呢？
劳森是一名有能力的大奖赛车手？不，不是这个。这本来也太明显了。一两场比赛无法改变这种看法。他职业生涯所做的一切已经足够说明问题。
这也不能证明他注定会赢得世界冠军。毕竟一个周末就只是一个周末。你需要大得多的样本才能下这个结论。
这甚至不能作为证据，去支持“如果当初让他继续驾驶小红牛21，他本可以扭转2025赛季”的说法。因为无论怎样，他的赛季本会变成一场持续的噩梦，这一点看起来和这个周末之前一样可能——这都是由他所处的环境造成的。
劳森被提拔到红牛时，总共只参加过11场一级方程式比赛，分散在两年里的两段短暂时期中，而且他被扔进了一辆多年来完全围绕维斯塔潘打造和研发的赛车。
劳森排位赛正好处在维斯塔潘身后，甚至在第一圈就和这位荷兰车手展开了缠斗。
赞德福特赛道或许恰恰证明了这一点：小红牛21与其说适合他的驾驶风格，程度大概就像奥康的赛车服穿在角田裕毅身上那么合身——或者甚至应该反过来说才对。
他几乎毫无经验，却被那些老板们置于巨大的压力之下——而那些老板当时之所以选择劳森，似乎仅仅是因为他们更不信任角田裕毅——他几乎注定要失败，而且不可否认，他失败得相当惨烈。但这也发生在他从未在一级方程式比赛中跑过的赛道上，此前还经历了一场艰难的季前测试，同时还要面对由红牛自己推波助澜的无休止的媒体审视。
在三次未能逃出第一节排位赛（其中包括在中国冲刺赛周末两次排位垫底）、并且不可避免地一分未得之后，他被扫地出门。在墨尔本的湿滑赛道上他还发生了一次事故，但公平地说，那天出事撞车的并非只有他一个。不过，缺乏速度这一点确实令人瞠目。

如今，在表面上看甚至更加不利的情况下——周一才接到通知，出发前往荷兰之前才进行了一次模拟器测试，而且只有一节自由练习赛来适应一辆全新的赛车——劳森的这个周末近乎完美。你可以说他没能在周五晚上的冲刺排位赛中晋级前三名排位赛（SQ3）是他的责任，但就连赫尔穆特·马尔科可能也不会怪他。在正赛排位赛中，劳森与维斯塔潘的差距仅为0.115秒，而在正赛中，他最终是唯一拿到积分的红牛车手——而且这个周末车队看起来也没比他最终的第7名有多少更多可取的东西了。

你可以用维斯塔潘被问到劳森排位赛表现时的说法来解释这一切。这位荷兰人的理论契合了他今年一贯的说法：2026年的F1赛车缺陷太大，以至于最好的车手也无法拉开多大差距。几小时后被问到这一理论的安德烈亚·斯特拉则委婉地表示不同意，他指出今年的技术太过复杂，微小的差异实际上反而会造成更大的差距。但很可能两个人其实都是对的。在2025年初交给劳森的那辆小红牛21上，维斯塔潘确实能产生巨大的影响——而第二辆车由谁来开其实并不重要。塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯在2024年底驾驶小红牛20时的表现也好不到哪儿去。后来角田裕毅也一样。
那么，劳森在赞德沃特的这个周末到底证明了什么？证明劳森能做得和伊萨克·哈贾尔一样好吗？不，这一点我们去年就看过了。也许它证明了同一位车手在拥有更多F1经验之后能更好地应对这样的挑战？嗯，这一点除了赫尔穆特·马尔科和克里斯蒂安·霍纳之外，恐怕对所有人来说都相当显而易见。
也许唯一真正能得出的结论是：红牛一年半前那些仓促的车手决定，确实和当时看起来一样疯狂。而且失败的并不是劳森——而是那些做出决定的人。
2025年3月，在解释这一决定时，赫尔穆特·马尔科指出，红牛并不是简单地把劳森降级回 青训车队（初级车队）——而是在拯救他的职业生涯。然而，如果当初没有被置于一个几乎没有回报的位置上，他的职业生涯或许根本不需要被拯救。
对劳森来说，这一切令人苦涩的地方在于，他在赞德沃特的表现可能对他的未来前景没有太大帮助。是的，他的2027年席位尚未确定——但他此前在小红牛已经干得足够扎实，本来有相当大的机会再赢得一年。这个周末会让他重新回到争夺红牛“大牌”席位的人选之列吗？嗯，随着马尔科已经离开，你很难想象哈贾尔会在没有明显理由的情况下被砍掉。
这个故事中还不可避免地存在“本可以怎样”的部分。如果红牛在2025赛季前的冬天做出了合乎逻辑的决定，那辆带毒性的小红牛21很可能从一开始就属于角田裕毅。劳森本可以在法恩扎车队再待一年，甚至有可能在2026年坐到维斯塔潘旁边——开一辆友好得多的赛车，带着多得多的经验，而且没有在红牛“失败”的污名。
然而，毫无疑问，这个周末对劳森本人来说非常重要。不是因为他向自己证明了什么。他大概早就知道自己是一名有能力的大奖赛车手。他说，他知道如果2025年获得更多时间，自己最终本会有更好的表现。他比任何人都清楚，在那两场比赛中，他面对的是一项几乎不可能完成的任务。
其他人可能有不同的看法。
2026年的赞德沃特只是让他们显得很可笑。
detailEn: Liam Lawson finally got his 'what could have been' moment

Liam Lawson's third race at Red Bull was exactly what Red Bull would have wanted from Liam Lawson. Solid qualifying, right behind Max Verstappen. No big mistakes and strong pace in the race. Points. He finally proved he deserved to be in that seat...
It's just that his third race at Red Bull wasn't Suzuka in April 2025, but Zandvoort some 17 months later.
So, how should we interpret Lawson's weekend? And what does it actually prove?
That Lawson is a capable grand prix driver? No, not that. That's too obvious anyway. One or two races can't change that perception. Everything he's done during his career is enough.
It doesn't prove he's destined to win the world championship either. One weekend is one weekend, after all. You'd need a much broader sample.

It can't even be used as evidence to back the claim that he could have turned his 2025 campaign around had he been given the chance to keep driving the RB21. Because it still looks as likely as it did before this weekend that his season would have turned into a continuous nightmare, no matter what – because of the circumstances he was dealing with.

Lawson was promoted to Red Bull with just 11 F1 races under his belt, spread across two short stints over two years, and thrown into a car that had been built and developed completely around Verstappen over the years.
Lawson qualified right behind Verstappen and even battled with the Dutchman on lap one
What Zandvoort probably proves is that the RB21 did indeed suit his driving style about as well as Esteban Ocon's overalls would fit Yuki Tsunoda – or perhaps even the other way around.

With almost no experience and put under enormous pressure by bosses who seemingly only chose Lawson back then because they believed in Tsunoda even less, he was almost destined to fail – and, there's no denying it, he did so spectacularly. But it also happened at tracks he had never raced at in F1, following a difficult pre-season test, while being exposed to relentless media scrutiny fuelled by Red Bull itself.

He was shown the door after failing to escape Q1 three times – including qualifying last twice on the sprint weekend in China – and inevitably scoring zero points. There was also an accident in Melbourne on a damp track, but he wasn't the only one crashing out that day, to be fair. The lack of pace, though, was just staggering.

Now, in what on the face of it were even worse circumstances – with a call on Monday, a simulator session right before his departure to the Netherlands and only one free practice session to adapt to a completely new machine – Lawson's weekend was near-perfect. You can pin the blame on him for not progressing into SQ3 on Friday evening in sprint qualifying, but even Helmut Marko probably wouldn't. Lawson's gap to Verstappen in main qualifying was a tiny 0.115s, and in the race he ultimately was the only Red Bull driver to score points – and it didn't look like there was a lot more on the table for the team this weekend than his eventual P7.

You can explain it the way Verstappen did when he was asked about Lawson's qualifying performance. The Dutchman's theory suits his narrative this year: F1 2026 is so flawed that the best drivers can't make as much of a difference. Andrea Stella, who was presented with that theory a few hours later, tactfully disagreed, noting that the technology is so complex this year that tiny differences can actually result in bigger gaps. But it may well be that both are actually right. In the RB21 Lawson was handed at the start of 2025, Verstappen indeed could make a huge difference – and it didn't really matter who was driving the second car. Sergio Perez at the end of 2024 wasn't really a lot better at the wheel of the RB20. Neither was Tsunoda later.

So, what did Lawson's Zandvoort weekend really prove? That Lawson can do as good a job as Isack Hadjar? No, we saw that last year. Maybe it proves that the same driver with considerably more Formula 1 experience can deal with such a challenge better? Well, that was probably fairly obvious to everyone apart from Helmut Marko and Christian Horner anyway.

Maybe the only real takeaway is that Red Bull's hectic driver decisions a year and a half ago were indeed as insane as they looked back then. And that it wasn't Lawson who failed – it was those making the calls.

In March 2025, explaining the decision, Helmut Marko pointed out that Red Bull wasn't simply demoting Lawson back to the junior team – it was saving his career instead. Yet his career perhaps wouldn't have needed any saving had he not been put in a position from which he had almost nothing to gain in the first place.

What's bitter for Lawson in all of this is that his Zandvoort performance probably isn't going to do much for his future prospects. No, his 2027 seat isn't confirmed yet - but he was already doing a solid enough job with Racing Bulls to have a fair chance of earning another year. Will this weekend put him back in contention for the "big" Red Bull seat? Well, with Marko not around anymore, you wouldn't really expect Hadjar to get axed for no apparent reason.

There's an inevitable 'what could have been' part of the story as well. Had Red Bull acted logically in the winter leading up to the 2025 season, the poisoned RB21 would probably have been Tsunoda's to take from the start. Lawson would have got another year with the Faenza squad and potentially could have started 2026 next to Verstappen – in a much friendlier car, with a lot more experience. And without the stigma of having 'failed' at Red Bull.

Yet, no doubt, this weekend was very important for Lawson himself. Not because he proved something to himself. He probably knew he was a capable grand prix driver. He says he knew he'd eventually have done better had he been given more time in 2025. He is aware, more than anyone, that he faced an almost impossible task in the two races he was given.
Others might have had different opinions.
Zandvoort 2026 just makes them look silly.
